Community Concerns for follow-up
AWWU Plant and violations: Mario Croce and Sandy Baker provided presentation to GBOS at their
regular meeting Sept 21 2026 and are providing a plant tour on October 19 at 10AM.

Levy and drainage concerns in Old Girdwood: ongoing discussions at state and city level regarding
flooding concerns of the levy from runoff and culverts that drain into Turnagain Arm. Community
discussions at PSAC, GHEC, Land Use and GBOS. Watershed Study for Girdwood has been added to
the MOA Watershed study list. Status of this study is on the agenda for MOA GBOS Quarterly meeting
Oct 26.

DOT Items:
DOT Alyeska Highway Pedestrian Safety Corridor (Bike Path) concerns:
Refresh of painted stencils: GVSA manager has approval from DOT for approval for GVSA to re-paint
stencils. Bollards: GVSA will continue to use bollards seasonally to restrict vehicles from path. Bollards
are removed in winter to allow for snow clearing.

GVSA does not have authority or funding mechanism to work on DOT ROW without permission by
DOT. Directive to lower the speed limit to 40MPH zone and extend the 30MPH zone, pending
information on timeline and infrastructure countermeasures by DOT to support these changes.

Community interest in traffic calming in the 45MPH zone: request to lower speed limit to 30MPH and
to add flashing radar “You are Speeding” signage. GBOS resolution of Support was recommended by
PSAC in November 2024; resolution 2025-03 was signed and sent to SOA in Jan 2025.

Airport:
Info provided at GBOS in September is:
As an unmanned airport, DOT says that the Emergency Response Plan for the airport is a matter to be
established between the airport Manager (DOT manager for Girdwood is Paul Berthall) and Fire Dept.
Airport Master Plan is due however was postponed due to budget constraints in 2026. DOT Airports
division is working through other Master Plan efforts, Girdwood Airport remains on the list for Master
Plan.

Unrestricted access to airport property. Public should call police to report illegal activity. No
recreational access is permitted on airport land.

Enforcement Concerns:
Drug/Alcohol use in Girdwood Parks – increased visibility by police
Alyeska Highway Speeding – increased enforcement.
Unsafe parking on roads - Call Whittier Police for parking enforcement if emergency vehicles are
unable to pass. WPD has authority to enforce municipal parking laws.

Homeless Camps:
Abatement of homeless camps completed spring 2024.
Healthy spaces team can be called for cleanup on public land: Report Camp or Trash Concern

PSAC Outreach:
PSAC has new QR code for public to scan and access the PSAC MOA webpage.
